references.text: Heshbon is mentioned as a city in the territory of the tribe of Reuben, bordering on Gad's land described in Joshua 13:26
Heshbon is noted as one of the cities east of the Jordan that the tribes of Gad and Reuben wished to settle in
Mahanaim is first mentioned here where Jacob met God's angels, the same place that forms the boundary in Joshua 13:26
Mahanaim later became the capital of Ish-Bosheth, Saul's son, highlighting the site's strategic importance
David fled to Mahanaim during Absalom's rebellion, confirming the city's significance within Gad's territory
Mahanaim was the seat of one of Solomon's twelve officials, demonstrating its continued administrative importance
Mizpah (Ramath-Mizpeh) is mentioned in connection with the covenant between Jacob and Laban, the same area as the boundary in Joshua 13:26
Mizpah in Gilead is mentioned in relation to Jephthah, referring to the same geographical region
